data.name: Aabad
data.gender_notes: Aabad is used as a male name in islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From Persian ābād (آباد) 'inhabited, cultivated, prosperous', itself from āb (آب) 'water'. It is NOT related to the Arabic ʿabd (عبد) 'servant' - that is the separate name ʿĀbid / Abid. Ābād is a productive Persian/Urdu toponymic element (Islāmābād, Ḥaydarābād, Abbottābād). Aabad therefore means “Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing”. Persian/Urdu toponymic and personal-name element; cf. Middle Persian ābād 'populous, thriving, prosperous'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aabad expresses “Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.

faq.q: Is Aabad related to the Arabic name Abid?
faq.a: No. Aabad comes from Persian ābād 'inhabited, cultivated, prosperous'. Abid (عابد) is a different Arabic name meaning 'worshipper', from the root ʿ-b-d. The two are unrelated despite the similar English spelling.

faq.q: What does the Persian word ābād mean?
faq.a: Ābād (آباد) is a Persian word meaning 'inhabited, cultivated, prosperous, thriving'. It is built on āb (آب) 'water' and is widely used as a place-name suffix across Iran, Pakistan and India.

faq.q: What does the name Aabad mean?
Where does the name Aabad come from?
What is the linguistic root of Aabad?
faq.a: The root of Aabad is Persian ābād (آباد), from āb (آب) 'water'.

faq.q: How is Aabad written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aabad is written آباد in Arabic script.

faq.q: Is Aabad a boy's or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aabad is used as a male name.

faq.q: Does Aabad appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aabad is not a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aabad verified?
faq.a: Yes — the meaning “Inhabited; cultivated; prosperous; flourishing” is established by Persian/Urdu toponymic and personal-name element; cf. Middle Persian ābād 'populous, thriving, prosperous'..
